findings.reason: The original standalone tiles have correct text rendering but no geometric explanation of the two meridian slopes. Paired torus fundamental domains materially clarify how the original meridian becomes a diagonal of longitudinal displacement +1 or -1 under the annular shear. A useful explanatory figure is warranted independently of the complete proof.
findings.action: Added paired TikZ fundamental squares in a final Remarks section, retaining the original meridian dashed and the two replacement meridians solid; signs label the induced boundary shear in proof 2.1.

correction: Added only an explanatory Remarks paragraph and a two-panel TikZ illustration of the annular-framing boundary slopes. All original source bytes, including the full frontmatter, Statement, Facts and Proof, remain the exact prefix of the current carrier.

source_lines_after.description: Added Remarks and paired meridian-shear figure

diagram_math_checks.data: The object in each panel is the boundary torus of the tubular neighbourhood N(K); each square identifies opposite sides. The horizontal basis class is the annular parallel lambda_A, and vertical basis class is the normal-disk meridian mu.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Proof 1.1 constructs K, N(K), A, lambda_A and the disk-bounding meridian. The Heegaard supplier specifies phi: boundary H_- to boundary H_+; the figure stays on boundary N(K) and does not alter or reverse that interface.

diagram_math_checks.data: The original dashed vertical segment has displacement (0,1) in the (lambda_A,mu) basis. The left solid segment has displacement (1,1), hence mu+lambda_A. The right solid segment is directed from lower right to upper left and has displacement (-1,1), hence mu-lambda_A. Each closes on the torus after opposite-side identification.
diagram_math_checks.justification: These are exactly the two boundary homology shears of proof 2.1. Both retain coefficient +1 on mu. The diagonal directions were checked in the actual rendered native image.

diagram_math_checks.data: Both panels use lambda_A fixed and opposite one-turn shears of mu. In coordinates (x,y) along (lambda_A,mu), the shears are (x,y) -> (x+y,y) and (x,y) -> (x-y,y), inverse determinant-one transformations.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Proof 2.1 explicitly states longitude fixed and meridian image mu +/- lambda_A. The Dehn-twist supplier defines opposite turns by theta -> theta +/- 2 pi rho(t). The panels are labeled by their boundary shear, retaining the item's convention-dependent correspondence rather than introducing an ambient right-hand sign convention.

diagram_math_checks.data: Each replacement slope is primitive and has coefficient of magnitude 1 relative to the annulus framing. The illustration introduces no claim of a further framing shift.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Statement and proof 3.1 use these exact slopes to identify the filling with gluing phi composed with tau_c or its inverse. The rigorous construction in proof 1.1-4.1 is byte-unchanged and remains independent of the figure.

visual_check.result: Native TikZ compiled. Standalone original-resolution views show both square boundaries, both original-meridian dashed upward arrows, both directed solid diagonal curves, all positive-coordinate arrows and both slope labels without clipping or overlap.

evidence_path_resolution.reason: Declared supplemental screenshots were absent; authentic same-category screenshots were located and SHA256 checked against queue rows before viewing.
